standard.title: Reflect on media arts works to inform practice
standard.description: reflect on their own and others' media arts works and practices to inform choices they make during the production process
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can use feedback to reflect on own media arts practice (AC9AMA6D02). They have not yet investigated others' media arts works and practices systematically as a source of influence, or used structured reflection to document and direct production decisions.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students reflect on own and others' media arts works to make and document informed production choices throughout the production process.

nodes.label: Documenting and explaining creative choices
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can document and explain their creative choices in relation to representations, genre codes and conventions with reference to intended meaning
nodes.minimum_width: Document at least two creative choices in own media arts work; explain how each constructs a representation for the intended audience
nodes.typical_width: Document and explain creative choices throughout the production process in relation to representations, genre codes and conventions; use Viewpoints questions to interrogate own decisions
wider: Use Viewpoints questions to interrogate own representational choices — 'How can I represent a range of views?', 'What do I need to change to create stronger audience connection?' — document how each question drives production refinement
Use a storyboarding or editing template to annotate creative thinking — document the reasoning behind decisions, not just the decisions themselves
Develop a production journal that traces how creative choices have evolved across pre-production, production and post-production — evaluate what the documentation reveals about own decision-making

response_modes.reason: Documenting creative choices with genuine reasoning — explaining why a decision serves the intended representation rather than just recording what was decided — is a reflective practice habit that develops through sustained iteration. Students who document after the fact without reasoning through the decisions haven't built the habit of reflective production practice.

success_criteria: Documents at least two creative choices with reasoning
Explains how each choice constructs a representation for the intended audience
Documentation goes beyond 'I decided to...' — explains why the choice serves the intended meaning

nodes.label: Reflecting on audience engagement
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can reflect on potential audience engagement and use that reflection to refine production choices
nodes.minimum_width: Reflect on how at least one production choice affects potential audience engagement; document at least one refinement based on that reflection
nodes.typical_width: Consider potential audience engagement to inform refinements across the production process; use Viewpoints questions to evaluate how production choices create audience connection; document reasoning
wider: Justify decisions made by producers in the construction of representations — evaluate how technical and symbolic codes serve producer interests and audience positioning
Observe and consider how audience engagement would differ across different audience groups — evaluate how the same work could position different audiences differently
Investigate how media arts practitioners from other cultural contexts construct audience relationships — explore how cultural context shapes what 'engaging' means for different audiences

response_modes.reason: Students commonly make production choices without reasoning from the audience's perspective — they think about what they want to do rather than what the audience will receive. Scaffolding the audience perspective reasoning (who is my audience, how will they receive this choice, what does this choice communicate to them?) builds the habit of audience-centred production thinking.

success_criteria: Reflects on how at least one production choice affects audience engagement
Documents at least one refinement based on audience-centred reasoning
Reasoning is from audience perspective — not just own creative preference

nodes.label: Investigating others' practices to inform own
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can investigate other media arts works and practices and use insights to inform deliberate choices in own production
nodes.minimum_width: Investigate at least one other media arts work or practice; identify one specific insight that has informed a choice in own production
nodes.typical_width: Document and explain how investigating other media arts works and practices informs own representational choices; connect specific analytical observations to specific production decisions
wider: Explore styles and representations from another cultural context (e.g. cartooning genres in Asia) — use the investigation to inform own practice and develop understanding of cultural appropriation vs cross-cultural influence
Investigate how media arts conventions from different cultural contexts use technical codes differently — analyse what each convention communicates and how cultural context shapes its meaning
Develop a reflective account of how investigation of others' practices has changed own production approach across a unit — trace specific moments of influence

response_modes.reason: This node integrates documentation practice (Node 1), audience-centred reflection (Node 2), and analytical skills from E01 into a coherent account of how investigation informs production. Students who can analyse other works but cannot connect that analysis to own production decisions have not met the standard's full demand.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The cross-cultural media arts investigation direction is rich — investigating how cartooning or other media forms operate differently in Asian cultural contexts gives advancing students both expanded analytical vocabulary and a concrete case for thinking through cultural appropriation vs informed cross-cultural influence.
success_criteria: Investigates at least one other work or practice with a specific analytical focus
Connects the investigation to a specific production decision
Distinguishes informed influence from uncritical imitation or cultural appropriation
